How the campaign works

  1. Start with one finished block. A short orchard clip leads into the free one-page checklist.
  2. Ask a few questions before delivery. Growers tell us what they grow and roughly how much, then choose whether they want a callback or a link to the recorded discussion.
  3. Take relevant requests to Josh. Marketing screens requests before handing over the grower’s question and block context.

One-page grower checklist · draft

The last bin’s gone. Is the job done?

Pick one block that’s finished. Walk it while you can still see how the canopy is holding up. Use what came off the block to decide what’s worth another look.

If a block didn’t finish as expected or you’re unsure whether it’s still worth sampling, you can request a call with Josh or ask for the recorded discussion.

DSA, standard leaf testing and seasonal trends

Differential Sap Analysis (also called a Differential Leaf Extract Test) compares Nutrients in fluid extracted separately from young and older leaves collected together from the same block.

What the paired results add

Separate young and older leaf results help your agronomist investigate Nutrient concerns, prioritise follow-up and assess whether a prescription or its timing needs changing. The results are read with soil, water, crop growth and recent applications.

ComparisonStandard leaf tissue testDSA / paired-leaf sap analysis
SampleThe crop-specific leaf or plant part required by the laboratory.Young and older leaves collected together and kept as separately identified samples.
MeasurementNutrient concentrations in dried plant material, reported on a dry-matter basis.Nutrient concentrations in extracted leaf fluid, reported separately for each leaf age. The panel may also include sugars, pH and EC.
Useful forAssessing the sampled tissue against a suitable crop-stage reference and following consistent repeat samples.Comparing the two leaf ages at a crop stage, then following changes across comparable repeat pairs.

The methods can complement one another. Sampling protocols, units and reference values differ, so the numbers are not directly interchangeable. Neither test establishes the cause of a result on its own.

Build a seasonal record

A series of comparable DSAs at relevant crop stages builds a record of how the young and older leaf results change through the season. Read alongside applications, weather, crop load and harvest or quality records, it can help identify recurring Nutrient concerns and refine the following season’s timing and prescriptions.

Keep the crop-stage context when comparing results and seasons, and agree sampling frequency with your agronomist around useful decisions.

See page 3 of the three-page guide for the full comparison. Review the units, sampling context and permissions before using the historical Calcium chart. Keep any reference range tied to its report. Differences between leaf ages alone cannot show how a treatment changed the result.

Propose a seven-day Clicks pilot with an A$175 campaign total, plus applicable tax. Confirm account access, Australian location options, the accepted budget and the bid guidance in Ads Manager. Compare the two ads on a similar offer and stage.

Follow up as their blocks finish picking

Confirmed Cherry growers

Use the last pick and pack-out as the starting point. Where someone is still picking, share the checklist to keep and offer the callback after the block finishes.

Crop still unknown

Lead with “if you grow Cherries” and invite them to tell us what they grow. Send to the consented Cherry and unknown-crop groups only.

Use current crop information, enquiry history, channel consent and opt-outs. Match by enquiry ID, then normalised email and phone. The combined campaign’s 79 contacts are the starting records. Confirm the eligible send count and record re-engagement separately.

Look at the areas that finished differently and put what you see beside the pack-out and what you know about the block. We’ve put seven jobs on one page for you to take out into the orchard.”

Recorded interview and what to reuse

Josh recommends a recorded conversation using prepared questions and real observations from the orchard. Aim for a 25–30 minute first edit. An internal interviewer can get it started. Sarah Tinsley, Josh and Andrew were suggested in the longer draft, subject to availability.

  • Start with one block decision after the last pick. Show what changes between an active canopy and autumn colour.
  • Compare what leaf tissue and paired sap tests show. Use a cleared example alongside the block diary to explain what to check next.
  • Pull questions from the earlier webinars and from growers who respond to the form. Use the most relevant questions for winter and spring follow-up.

Nathan and Pia coordinate filming and editing, and turn the interview into a replay, short clips, an article, social posts and grower follow-up material. Josh supplies field observations and reviews technical wording. Andrew can show a Cherry example if available. Keep Josh’s fruit-fill scripts for an earlier crop stage.
